## Pre-Lab
1. Equation that relates $n$, $\theta$, $d$ and $\lambda$
   $$d sin(\theta) = n \lambda$$

1. Solving for 4000 and 440
   
$$d\sin(\theta) = n\lambda$$
$$\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{n\lambda}{d}\right)$$
$$d = \frac{1\text{ cm}}{4000} = \frac{0.01\text{ m}}{4000}$$
$$d = 2.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$$
$$n = 1$$
$$\lambda = 0.44 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$$
$$\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{1 \times 0.44 \times 10^{-6}}{2.5 \times 10^{-6}}\right)$$
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.176)$$
$$\theta \approx 10.14^\circ$$
